import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

COL = 64
WIDTH = 48
K = 16
HID = 16

RECIPE = {"ppo_epochs": 3}


class FootprintHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in footprints]
        n = len(self.fps)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, K * n, 1)
        self.anchor = nn.Conv2d(c, HID * n, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * K, HID, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.out = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = F.relu(self.proj(f))
        a = self.anchor(f)
        outs = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            pt = p[:, t * K:(t + 1) * K]
            if dy > 1 or dx > 1:
                pt = F.pad(pt, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(pt, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-pt, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(pt, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            else:
                mx = pt
                mn = pt
                av = pt
            h = F.relu(self.mix[t](torch.cat([mx, mn, av], 1)) + a[:, t * HID:(t + 1) * HID])
            outs.append(self.out[t](h))
        return torch.cat(outs, 1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.col = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, COL, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(COL, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.skip = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 1)
        self.head = FootprintHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        c = self.col(obs)
        h = F.relu(self.conv1(c))
        f = F.relu(self.conv2(h) + self.skip(c))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.hypothesis: The same 2D conv runs on every layer, with the layer folded into the batch. Its inputs are that layer's build, target, missing and extra channels, the same channels for the layers just below and above, a projection of the whole column, and a learned layer embedding. Each layer scores each brick placement with footprint pooling, and logsumexp over layers picks the landing-layer score. This matches the drop physics and shares weights across heights at about 2D cost (r≈1.4, ppo_epochs=3). Refuted if it does no better than the plain 2D conv candidates.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

W = 32
K = 8
HID = 8

RECIPE = {"ppo_epochs": 3}


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        n = len(self.fps)
        self.n = n
        self.glob_in = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, W, 1)
        self.layer_in = nn.Conv2d(12, W, 1)
        self.zemb = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(spec.Z, W) * 0.1)
        self.conv = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.pw = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 1)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(W, K * n, 1)
        self.anchor = nn.Conv2d(W, HID * n, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * K, HID, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.out = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(3 * W, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        per = torch.stack([obs[:, 0:Z], obs[:, Z:2 * Z], obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z], obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z]], 2)
        padded = F.pad(per, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1))
        below = padded[:, 0:Z]
        above = padded[:, 2:Z + 2]
        lay = torch.cat([per, below, above], 2).reshape(B * Z, 12, Y, X)
        g = self.glob_in(obs)
        h = self.layer_in(lay).view(B, Z, W, Y, X) + g.unsqueeze(1) + self.zemb.view(1, Z, W, 1, 1)
        h = F.relu(h).reshape(B * Z, W, Y, X)
        h = F.relu(self.conv(h))
        h = F.relu(self.pw(h) + h)
        p = F.relu(self.proj(h))
        a = self.anchor(h)
        outs = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            pt = p[:, t * K:(t + 1) * K]
            if dy > 1 or dx > 1:
                pt = F.pad(pt, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(pt, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-pt, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(pt, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            else:
                mx = pt
                mn = pt
                av = pt
            q = F.relu(self.mix[t](torch.cat([mx, mn, av], 1)) + a[:, t * HID:(t + 1) * HID])
            outs.append(self.out[t](q))
        s = torch.cat(outs, 1).view(B, Z, self.n, Y, X)
        place = torch.logsumexp(s, dim=1).flatten(1)
        hz = h.view(B, Z, W, Y, X)
        pooled = torch.cat([hz.mean((1, 3, 4)), hz.amax((1, 3, 4)), F.relu(g).mean((2, 3))], dim=1)
        gg = self.glob(pooled)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(gg)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(gg).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch

        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.R = 2 * spec.Z - 1
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        n = len(self.fps)
        self.n = n
        self.layer_in = nn.Conv2d(5 * self.R + 3, W, 1)
        self.zemb = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(spec.Z, W) * 0.1)
        self.conv = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.pw = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 1)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(W, K * n, 1)
        self.anchor = nn.Conv2d(W, HID * n, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * K, HID, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.out = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * W, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

            q = F.relu(self.mix[t](torch.cat([mx, mn, av], 1)) + a[:, t * HID:(t + 1) * HID])

        s = torch.cat(outs, 1).view(B, Z, self.n, Y, X)

        p = F.relu(self.proj(f))
        a = self.anchor(f)
        outs = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            pt = p[:, t * K:(t + 1) * K]
            if dy > 1 or dx > 1:
                pt = F.pad(pt, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(pt, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-pt, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(pt, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            else:
                mx = pt
                mn = pt
                av = pt
            h = F.relu(self.mix[t](torch.cat([mx, mn, av], 1)) + a[:, t * HID:(t + 1) * HID])
            outs.append(self.out[t](h))
        return torch.cat(outs, 1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.col = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, COL, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(COL, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.skip = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 1)
        self.head = FootprintHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        c = self.col(obs)
        h = F.relu(self.conv1(c))
        f = F.relu(self.conv2(h) + self.skip(c))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

                mx = F.max_pool2d(pt, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-pt, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(pt, (dy, dx), stride=1)

                mx = pt
                mn = pt
                av = pt
            h = F.relu(self.mix[t](torch.cat([mx, mn, av], 1)) + a[:, t * HID:(t + 1) * HID])
            outs.append(self.out[t](h))
        return torch.cat(outs, 1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.col = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, COL, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(COL, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.skip = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.bcast = nn.Linear(64, WIDTH)
        self.head = FootprintHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints)
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        c = self.col(obs)
        h = F.relu(self.conv1(c))
        f = F.relu(self.conv2(h) + self.skip(c))
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        f2 = F.relu(f + self.bcast(g).unsqueeze(2).unsqueeze(3))
        place = self.head(f2)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

W = 32
K = 8
HID = 8

RECIPE = {"ppo_epochs": 1, "n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ent_coef": 0.005, "gae_lambda": 0.95}


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        n = len(self.fps)
        self.n = n
        self.glob_in = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, W, 1)
        self.layer_in = nn.Conv2d(12, W, 1)
        self.zemb = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(spec.Z, W) * 0.1)
        self.conv = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.pw = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 1)
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(W, K * n, 1)
        self.anchor = nn.Conv2d(W, HID * n, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * K, HID, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.out = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(3 * W, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        per = torch.stack([obs[:, 0:Z], obs[:, Z:2 * Z], obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z], obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z]], 2)
        padded = F.pad(per, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1))
        below = padded[:, 0:Z]
        above = padded[:, 2:Z + 2]
        lay = torch.cat([per, below, above], 2).reshape(B * Z, 12, Y, X)
        g = self.glob_in(obs)
        h = self.layer_in(lay).view(B, Z, W, Y, X) + g.unsqueeze(1) + self.zemb.view(1, Z, W, 1, 1)
        h = F.relu(h).reshape(B * Z, W, Y, X)
        h = F.relu(self.conv(h))
        h = F.relu(self.pw(h) + h)
        p = F.relu(self.proj(h))
        a = self.anchor(h)
        outs = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.fps):
            pt = p[:, t * K:(t + 1) * K]
            if dy > 1 or dx > 1:
                pt = F.pad(pt, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(pt, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-pt, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(pt, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            else:
                mx = pt
                mn = pt
                av = pt
            q = F.relu(self.mix[t](torch.cat([mx, mn, av], 1)) + a[:, t * HID:(t + 1) * HID])
            outs.append(self.out[t](q))
        s = torch.cat(outs, 1).view(B, Z, self.n, Y, X)
        place = torch.logsumexp(s, dim=1).flatten(1)
        hz = h.view(B, Z, W, Y, X)
        pooled = torch.cat([hz.mean((1, 3, 4)), hz.amax((1, 3, 4)), F.relu(g).mean((2, 3))], dim=1)
        gg = self.glob(pooled)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(gg)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(gg).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no results yet. The budget is very tight: the default recipe gets about 131k steps, roughly 9k episodes and only 32 PPO updates. Any network more expensive than the starting one reduces the number of samples in proportion. Ratios near r≈1–1.5 are affordable; deep ResNets (r≥3) are not. Scores are hidden, so no trial can be credited for its result. Each candidate should therefore be a strong, well-argued bet on its own, and the candidates should differ from one another. The key perception for this task is layer by layer: where the brick lands (the highest build cell under its footprint), whether the target has every footprint cell at that layer, and whether placing it now seals cells the target still needs underneath. Two candidates build this in through allowed learned operations: a per-column MLP plus footprint pooling, and layer-shared 2D convolutions with a max over landing layers. The third keeps the starting network and tests a recipe with more samples and more updates.
analyses.2: Scores are hidden, so the only evidence is that all three round-1 files trained without errors and passed every check. Each run also tested only one idea. The footprint-pooled head (r1c1) fits the drop physics best. A brick's landing layer is the max height under its footprint, and an exact placement needs every footprint cell to match the target at that layer, which max/min pooling can learn. The layer-shared net (r1c2) puts this structure in directly. The recipe-only trial (r1c3) tests sample efficiency: with only about 131k samples and 32 updates, the default recipe may be the bottleneck. So in round 2 I combine the strongest-motivated architectures with the higher-sample recipe (ppo_epochs=2, n_envs=128, lower entropy, gae_lambda 0.95). I also test whether more capacity in the body and head is worth having fewer samples. Comparing A with B isolates the effect of capacity. Comparing C with A pits the layer-wise design against footprint pooling under the same recipe.
analyses.3: No scores are visible, so I have to rely on priors about the task. All six trials trained without errors. Placing a brick correctly means: its landing layer equals the target layer, every footprint cell is missing at that layer, and no target cell below it in those columns is still unbuilt (otherwise that cell is sealed forever). The footprint-pooling head (r1c1, r2c1) can represent this. The layer-shared net (r1c2, r2c3) fits it better, but its per-layer input sees only the layers just above and below, so it cannot easily learn the "nothing missing below" check. The sample-rich recipe (2 epochs, 128 envs) is the most plausible recipe base. Plan for this round: (1) a new layer-shared net whose per-layer input is a relative-height window over the whole column, so every layer gets the same column view; (2) r2c1 with twice as many PPO updates; (3) r2c1 with a longer horizon (gamma 0.99), so the bonus for an exact build counts for more against sealing mistakes.
analyses.4: Scores are hidden, so I can only reason from the task's structure and from which runs trained cleanly. All 9 trials ran without errors. The footprint-pooled head on a column-MLP and 3x3 conv body (r1c1, r2c1) is the most principled design for picking a brick and its landing spot. The sample-rich recipe (ppo_epochs 2, n_envs 128) trains on about 175k steps instead of about 118k. The layer-shared net (r1c2, r2c3) gives the cleanest physics prior at low cost. Two things remain untested. One is cutting PPO epochs further to buy more fresh designs: with fresh random targets, data diversity probably limits generalisation. The other is giving the placement head global context: build order depends on the whole design, not just a 5x5 neighbourhood. This is the last round and the final pick uses the top three dev scores, so each candidate is a plausible winner built on a proven base rather than a risky new idea.
